subject: Model slate prioritization & token snapshot — TalentWise onboarding
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@talentwise.com>
To: avery_johnson@redwood.com
Cc: Elena Rodriguez <elena@talentwise.com>
Date: 2028-07-22 09:12 -0700
Subject: Kickoff: model fit + token profile for TalentWise onboarding

Avery,

Thanks for the intro call earlier. As discussed, our immediate goal is to lock a small set of candidate models and get an initial token-volume snapshot so we can plan infra for our Q4 beta. High level context:
- Primary use cases: resume parsing + role matching + short follow-up Q&A (mostly conversational).
- Typical user session: 1-3 turns, average generated length ~120 tokens, occasional long context when parsing multi-section resumes (up to 6k chars).
- Expected traffic: pilot ~20k sessions/month; ramp to 200k sessions/month in 6 months.

Can you send a short list of model candidates with recommended context lengths and a rough token estimate (per request and monthly)? Also any risks we should flag (latency, cost hotspots, hot prefixes).

Appreciate it — can loop in procurement later.

Samir
Samir Patel
Head of ML Engineering
TalentWise
From: avery_johnson@redwood.com
To: Samir Patel <samir@talentwise.com>
Cc: Elena Rodriguez <elena@talentwise.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-22 11:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Kickoff: model fit + token profile for TalentWise onboarding

Samir — thanks, great context. I put together a short, pragmatic slate and a first-pass token snapshot attached (talentwise_token_snapshot.xlsx). Key takeaways up front:

1) Candidate models (prioritized for cost/latency vs. quality):
   - rw-mid-13B-8k: balanced option for QA+matching; supports 8k context which covers most resume scenarios without chunking. Expected latency ~120–200ms/token on Dedicated pools.
   - open-30B-q4-16k: better long-context handling for multi-section resumes; higher cost and slightly larger tail latency. Consider only for the parse endpoint (batch first).
   - rw-7B-4k-quant: very cost efficient for short-turn Q&A and reranking; limited for 6k resume blobs (would require prefix trimming).

2) Context strategy recommendation:
   - Two-endpoint approach: a) parse endpoint using open-30B-q4-16k in batch mode for full-document extraction (asynchronous), b) conversational endpoint using rw-mid-13B-8k for real-time matching and follow-ups.
   - If you want simpler infra initially, run single rw-mid-13B-8k and implement light chunking + KV cache for parsed sections.

3) Token estimates (sheet has line items) — summarized: 
   - Pilot (20k sessions/month), mixed profile: avg input 650 tokens, avg output 120 tokens -> ~15.4M tokens/month.
   - Mid ramp (200k sessions/month) -> ~154M tokens/month.
   - Parse-heavy scenario (10% of sessions trigger a full-document parse using 12k-in tokens) -> add ~24M tokens/month at pilot scale.

4) Operational notes / risks:
   - Hot prefixes: company-specific templates (cover letters) create repeated prefix cache hits — good for cost savings if cached, but watch for stale KV sizes.
   - Latency SLOs: conversational endpoint should aim for p95 < 350ms; we can meet this with rw-mid-13B on Dedicated or Hosted with reserved burst.
   - Cost levers: quantized 7B for non-latency-critical rerank steps; prefix caching for standard resume headers; batching for parse jobs.

Next steps I propose:
- Internal: Ben (cc'ed) to run a quick perf estimate on rw-mid-13B for your avg-turn sizes and return p50/p95 token-latency projections.
- External: Samir/Elena, confirm if you want the two-endpoint split (parse + conv) or start single-endpoint trial.

Attached: talentwise_token_snapshot.xlsx (breakdown by endpoint and traffic), model_shortlist_readme.pdf (rationale and fallback options).

Best,
Avery Johnson
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: avery_johnson@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@talentwise.com>, Elena Rodriguez <elena@talentwise.com>
Date: 2028-07-22 14:40 -0700
Subject: Re: Kickoff: model fit + token profile for TalentWise onboarding

Quick ops add from my side after skimming the sheet:

- I'll run a micro-benchmark on rw-mid-13B-8k with the following payloads: 1) 650-token input / 120-token output (conv) 2) 3-6k token resume parse payloads (batch). Will return p50/p95 ms/token and end-to-end latency estimates by tomorrow EOD PST.
- For the parse queue: recommend a job size cap of 64 sequences per batch to balance GPU utilization vs. tail latency; we should test 32/64/128.
- KV cache sizing: initial estimate (based on sample set) is ~2–4GB per instance if we keep long resume prefixes hot for 24 hours — I'll validate.
- Need confirmation if TalentWise is okay with asynchronous parse flow (webhook/callback) — that'll change SLOs and reduce real-time cost.

I'll attach benchmark notes once complete. If we go two-endpoint, engineering will want a quick runbook for fallbacks (e.g., auto-failover to quantized 7B for non-critical steps).

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Samir Patel <samir@talentwise.com>
To: avery_johnson@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: Elena Rodriguez <elena@talentwise.com>, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-23 14:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Kickoff: model fit + token profile for TalentWise onboarding

Thanks, Avery and Ben — this is exactly what we needed to move forward. We agree to start with the two-endpoint split you suggested: async parse (batch) + real-time conv. A few quick confirmations:
- Async parse: TalentWise is fine with webhook callbacks for parse completion.
- Pilot traffic schedule: we'll start internal beta Aug 15 with ~20k sessions/month.
- Security: we will send the SOC 2 questionnaire and our procurement team will start the review — Monica, you'll be our contact for contract/proc.

Next asks: can you share a stripped sample of the token_snapshot (anonymized totals) for our procurement and infra teams? We need the high-level monthly token bands and a 3-month cost ballpark for both single-endpoint and two-endpoint options.

I'll calendar a check-in for Aug 1 to see the benchmark numbers.

Samir

-- End of thread --
